content_voiceover: Here's a board style question on the new ICC classification of B-lymphoblastic leukemia. It asks which prognostic statement is wrong. Option A is correct as written, since MYC rearranged B-ALL typically shows unmutated immunoglobulin heavy chain variable genes, unlike high grade B-cell lymphomas with MYC rearrangement, which usually show somatic hypermutation, reflecting a germinal center origin. Option B is also correct, since DUX4 rearranged ALL is a relatively common pediatric subtype and carries an excellent prognosis despite often being cryptic on standard karyotype. Option C correctly describes BCR colon colon ABL1 positive ALL as splitting into two biologically distinct groups, one with lymphoid only involvement and one with multilineage involvement resembling a stem cell process. Option E is correct too, since MEF2D rearranged B-ALL is recognized as a poor risk subtype with a tendency to relapse. That leaves option D as the wrong statement, since B-ALL with t twelve twenty one, involving ETV6 RUNX1, is actually a favorable, good risk subtype, not a poor risk one, making it the correct answer to select as the false statement.
keypoints: ETV6 RUNX1 t(12;21) B-ALL is good risk, not poor risk, making option D the wrong statement
MYC rearranged B-ALL has unmutated IGHV genes, unlike MYC rearranged high grade B-cell lymphoma
DUX4 rearranged ALL is common in children and has an excellent prognosis
BCR-ABL1 positive ALL splits into lymphoid only versus multilineage involvement subsets
MEF2D rearranged B-ALL is a poor risk subtype
keypoint_voiceover: The key trap here is remembering that ETV6 RUNX1 fusion from t twelve twenty one is a favorable marker in B-ALL, so calling it poor risk is the wrong statement and the correct exam answer. Keep straight that MYC rearranged B-ALL has unmutated immunoglobulin genes while MYC rearranged lymphoma shows hypermutation. Remember DUX4 rearranged ALL is common in kids with a great outcome, BCR-ABL1 positive ALL divides into lymphoid only and multilineage forms, and MEF2D rearrangement carries a poor prognosis.
